The API surface should either be cleaned up (remove from header) or the documentation should clearly state it's deprecated and ignored.; file: core/include/ecuio/core.h; quote: ecuio_status_t ecuio_init(void);

questions: Does profile_registry.cpp or any other core code have hidden dependencies on g_initialized being set? The diff removes it but I don't see verification that all such dependencies are eliminated.

Is there a thread-safety concern with the profile registry's function-local static if multiple threads might access it before initialization? The comment mentions C++11 magic statics but the core should be verified for thread-safety without init.

Why does the QML layer still have Bridge.connecting and Bridge.disconnecting properties that the diff references, but there's no indication of how these relate to the removed coreInitialized property?
nits: The comment in profile.h says 'Built-ins are always present (initialized on first registry access; core needs no ecuio_init, core.h)' but this is a comment about the built-ins, not about the profile registry's thread-safety guarantees.
The diff removes m_initialized from qttunebridge.h but doesn't update any comments that might reference it.
Consider adding a static_assert or runtime check in core.cpp to verify that the profile registry works without ecuio_init being called first.
